title: Beyond Matryoshka: Revisiting Sparse Coding for Adaptive Representation
reviewed_version: Published ICML2025 PMLR267 19-page PDF; repository b284898cc5c6ea6776772ca2c460a53badc6fe65
summary: The spectral NCL identifiability theorem is transferred without justification to CSR's different loss. Literal and normalized readings were checked, including an explicit reconstruction-compatible ambiguity.
limitations: No author-code execution or empirical timing/accuracy reproduction.
Not a refutation of the cited theorem under its own spectral assumptions.
No later-version or global erratum search.
The normalized ambiguity is for the paper's reconstruction equations plus normalized contrastive loss; no full released-pipeline global-minimum claim.

problems.source_claim: CSR Eq6 can invoke Wang et al. Theorem5 and theoretically guarantee identifiability/disentanglement and increased latent utilization.
problems.location: PDF p5 Section3.2.2 Eq6/Theorem5 and surrounding text; p7 Section4.4
assumptions: CSR nonnegative TopK+ReLU features, at most k active coordinates
Literal Eq6 is unnormalized; the normalized contrastive reading is checked with the paper's reconstruction equations, not the full released training pipeline
For normalized construction: d2,h8,k2,4k8,batch2,k_aux1, zero biases, tied decoder; both encoders exact-reconstruct inputs e1,e2
Finite example does not claim to satisfy the original theorem's distinct spectral setting
problems.check: Original reference theorem applies to spectral NCL with latent-class conditions. Literal Eq6 gives log(1+exp(-a^2)) and no finite contrastive minimizer. Normalized sparse encoders A and B have same Gram I, zero reconstruction, same loss, but different nonzero counts and cannot be equivalent under invertible diagonal scaling/permutation.
problems.result: Claimed inheritance is invalid. Added-loss empirical benefits can survive.
problems.counterevidence: Released code normalizes features and uses two duplicate views, defeating the unnormalized scale-escape criticism alone. The normalized ambiguity concerns that contrastive reading combined with paper Eq5. Optional input preprocessing and residual-variance-normalized auxiliary loss in the release prevent treating the zero-residual example as a full executable-pipeline optimizer. The original spectral theorem is not refuted.
problems.core_dependency: Identifiability is presented as the theoretical guarantee motivating the central sparse contrastive component and explaining dead-latent reduction.
problems.impact: Major; no change in benchmark score asserted.

correction.reason: An actual-objective theorem would be needed.
